definition: Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer — Google’s unified framework casting every NLP task as text-to-text, with the encoder-decoder models of the same name.
details: Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer — Google’s unified framework casting every NLP task as text-to-text, with the encoder-decoder models of the same name.

explainer.lead: T5 (Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer) is Google's unified framework that casts every NLP task as text-to-text, along with the encoder-decoder models of the same name. It matters because one formulation covers many tasks.

tiers.eli5: Whatever you want done with words, you phrase it as text going in and text coming out, and the same machine handles it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers frame each NLP task as text input producing text output, then use the encoder-decoder models of the same name. The pitfall is that the uniform framing does not by itself guarantee quality on any particular task.
tiers.paperLevel: A framework treating every NLP task as text-to-text, with encoder-decoder models of the same name. Limits: it is a formulation and model family, not a task-specific guarantee.

explainer.example: Both translation and summarization are expressed the same way: input text in, output text out, handled by the same model family.
